Nina Park: :rotating_light: paging - se-rt2 observing KV cache eviction queue overflow; continuous-batcher backlog climbing rapidly, io-wait high on gpu-pool-2. Seems correlated with the tokenizer-v3 rollout + new batch.multitenancy flag. Paging @oncall-bot.
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-158 · Severity: P2 · Pager: @oncall-bot (routing to Ravi Kumar). See: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-158
Ravi Kumar: Acknowledged. Nina, paste recent error snippets and the config changes that deployed around 14:12.
Nina Park: Logs: ```
[14:13:05] kv_cache.size=2.9GB
[14:13:05] eviction.queue.len=0/0 (overflow)
[14:13:06] continuous-batcher.pending=1450
[14:13:07] prefix_key_mismatch=1024
[14:14:12] p95_latency=2.1s p99=7.4s
[14:14:20] write_rate spikes -> 8x baseline
```
Deployed diff (14:10): ```diff
+ batch.multitenancy.enabled=true
+ batch.max_concurrency=128
- prefix_cache.hash_algo=blake2b
+ prefix_cache.hash_algo=md5
+ prefix_cache.normalization=off
```
Zoe Becker: md5 + normalization off is suspicious. Also batch.multitenancy increases the number of distinct prefix contexts, multiplicatively increasing prefix writes.
Sam Patel: Early hypothesis: tokenizer-v3 changed token boundaries; combined with multitenancy and md5 switch we generated a flood of distinct keys. Eviction subsystem expects normalized fixed-length hex; with normalization off some keys were written with mixed-case hex strings and evictor treats them as different entries and doesn't find the matching TTL entries. That prevents eviction -> cache size grows until eviction queue gets starved.
Ravi Kumar: Mitigation tasks: 1) disable batch.multitenancy flag for se-rt2 2) revert prefix_cache.hash_algo to blake2b 3) enable normalization and force TTL on writes 4) impose emergency qps limit on continuous-batcher 5) schedule safe scrub of suspect keyspace.
Nina Park: Kicking step 1 now: ```bash
./feature-flag set --env=se-rt2 --flag=batch.multitenancy.enabled --value=false --service=continuous-batcher
```
oncall-bot: @Ravi Kumar acknowledged the pager (ETA 20m).
Ravi Kumar: Applying step 2/3 now and adding a temporary write-side guard to set TTL if absent. Patch snippet to inject (hot reload): ```go
func WritePrefix(key string, val []byte) error {
  k := normalizeHex(key) // force lowercase, pad to fixed length
  if ttl := extractTTL(); ttl == 0 { ttl = defaultTTL }
  return cache.Set(k, val, ttl)
}
```
Ravi Kumar: Also injecting batch limiter: ```yaml
continuous-batcher:
  qps_limit: 800
  concurrency: 48
```
Nina Park: Changes pushed. Monitoring charts show write-rate falling to 1.5x baseline, pending queue down to 260. p95 improving to ~620ms.
Zoe Becker: Looking at eviction logs - confirm eviction requests were generated but failed to match keys due to mixed-case hex and missing zero-padding. The md5 switch produced shorter hex on some codepaths; normalization off means we wrote both "pref:1a2b" and "pref:001A2B" and they don't unify.
Sam Patel: Customer impact: initial spike affected notebot-inc and mapsly-prod, causing degraded responses and occasional 502s. I sent a heads-up to account teams and created a status page note.
incident-bot: INC-2026-158 updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Owner: Ravi Kumar.
Ravi Kumar: Plan for scrub: perform a staged key rewrite + delete of orphaned variants. First dry-run to map duplicate keys: ```bash
python tools/prefix_key_mapper.py --env=se-rt2 --prefix "pref:" --window 24h --dry-run=true --out=keymap.json
```
Zoe Becker: Running mapper now (dry-run). Early pass shows ~27k suspected duplicate key groups in last 24h. Will convert in small batches to avoid IO spikes.
Nina Park: Deploy hotfix PR to runtime to always normalize keys and set TTL on write: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/7912 - includes a migration utility to rewrite keys in-place.
Ravi Kumar: Agree on immediate follow-ups: 1) revert md5/hash change in config 2) add canary tests for prefix key compatibility when changing tokenizer or hashing 3) metric to alert on prefix-key churn > 5k/min 4) circuit-breaker to auto-disable prefix_cache if eviction failure rate exceeds threshold.
Sam Patel: Noted. Customer metrics: error rate for affected tenants down from 4.1% -> 0.4% after throttle + revert. Some residual slow tails; recommended SRE maintain monitoring for 3 hours.
Zoe Becker: Starting safe rewrite at +20m: rewriting keys by mapping mixed-case/padded forms to normalized form and merging TTLs. Command: ```bash
python tools/prefix_key_rewrite.py --env se-rt2 --prefix "pref:" --batch 300 --merge-ttl --dry-run=false
```
Nina Park: I'm handling outbound comms for Notebot and Mapsly; will share timeline and mitigation steps.
Ravi Kumar: Handoff: Li away, leaving Zoe as primary monitor; I will remain reachable for escalations for 45m. oncall-bot, mark handoff.
oncall-bot: @Zoe Becker acknowledged the handoff.
Zoe Becker: First rewrite pass complete: merged 26,743 duplicate variants over 22 minutes. Memory and eviction queue returned to healthy ranges. Will run a second pass focusing on older 48h window.
Nina Park: Final metrics snapshot (15:05): kv_cache.size 420MB, continuous-batcher.pending 18, p95_latency 210ms, error_rate 0.2%.
Sam Patel: Recording post-incident actions: rollback md5, add preflight validator for hash+tokenizer compatibility, add prefix churn alert, implement circuit-breaker. Owner assignments to follow.
incident-bot: INC-2026-158 marked resolved -> postmortem required. Postmortem link: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-158/postmortem
Ravi Kumar: Thanks team. Zoe, please compile timeline and attach key maps. I'll draft technical remediation notes.
Zoe Becker: Will do. Closing channel monitoring but will keep watch on dashboards for 3 hours. :white_check_mark:
